tools.name: screen_numbers
tools.description: Screen UK phone numbers against the TPS and CTPS registers before calling. Each result is clean, tps-listed, ctps-listed, unknown, suppressed or consented. Draws the account's prepaid UK credits, one per distinct valid number; a test API key (tpsc_test_) returns fixtures at no cost. Same as POST /v1

tools.name: wash_au_numbers
tools.description: Wash Australian phone numbers against the Do Not Call Register. Needs a live account (an OAuth sign-in or a tpsc_live_ key), as the register has no test mode. One prepaid AU wash per distinct valid number; invalid numbers cost nothing and numbers the register gave no answer for are refunded. Same as

tools.name: check_dead_numbers
tools.description: Live mobile network (HLR) lookups: whether each mobile is live, switched off or dead. Needs a live account (an OAuth sign-in or a tpsc_live_ key). One prepaid dead number check per mobile, two for a US number; numbers that are not mobiles and invalid numbers cost nothing. Same as POST /v1/dead-numbe

tools.name: get_account

tools.name: set_company_name
tools.description: Set the legal name of the business this account screens numbers for (PATCH /v1/me). Required before a live key can screen. tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: Creates a Stripe Checkout payment link for a prepaid pack on the connected account and returns the URL. tools.name: list_packs
tools.description: Every prepaid pack on sale: its id (the one buy_credits takes), name, what it buys, price in minor units ex VAT, currency and how many months the credits last. Optionally filter by kind. Costs nothing.

tools.name: get_screening_history
tools.description: The account's recent activity, newest first: each UK screening call (time, environment, numbers checked, counts by outcome, campaign_ref, request_id) and each movement on the UK credit, AU wash and dead number balances (purchases, draws, refunds). findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "screen_numbers" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Screen UK phone numbers against the TPS and CTPS registers before calling. Each result is clean, tps-listed, ctps-listed, unknown, suppressed or consented. Draw…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "buy_credits" is 1712 chars, far longer than this server's median (330). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_dead_numbers · Private data: screen_numbers, set_company_name · Public sink: screen_numbers, wash_au_numbers, check_dead_numbers.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_dead_numbers · Private data: screen_numbers, set_company_name · Public sink: screen_numbers, wash_au_numbers, check_dead_numbers

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "screen_numbers" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
